input.strategy_title: Feature Store as a supported RHOAI component
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Customers building recommendation and fraud models ask for a supported feature
store; today they self-manage upstream Feast next to the platform with no
lifecycle integration, no supported images, and no UI presence. Feast has a
Jira component reserved (Feature Store) but is not yet part of the platform:
there is no productized repository, no build pipeline, and no operator
integration. This strategy brings Feast in as a supported, installable RHOAI
component.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Administrators can enable a supported Feature Store (Feast) through the Platform Operator like any other managed component, with productized images. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Data scientists can reach the feature store from workbenches with the Feast SDK preinstalled in at least one supported workbench image. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | The Dashboard shows the Feature Store as an enabled component and links users to its endpoints per project. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Product documentation covers enablement, a getting-started walkthrough, and supported limits. |

## Affected Components

- Feature Store
- Dashboard
- Platform Operator
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- A feature-authoring UI in the Dashboard (link-out only this release)
- Managed offline-store infrastructure — customers bring their own storage

## Open Questions

1. Which Feast deployment topology do we productize first — the operator-based
   deployment or the standalone server per project? Upstream supports both;
   supportability differs.

# Productize the operator-based Feast deployment

## Description

Conditional branch (outcome A of the deployment-topology investigation): if the
operator-based topology is selected, productize the Feast operator deployment —
container images, CRDs, and deployment resources — in the midstream Feast
repository. If the investigation selects the standalone-server topology
instead, this epic is dropped and that branch applies.

## Scope

- Build and publish the Feast operator and related container images from the
  midstream Feast repository through the Konflux pipeline.
- Carry the CRDs and deployment resources for the operator-based deployment.
- Make the deployment consumable by the Platform Operator enablement
  integration (the managed-component enablement drives this deployment).
- Pin productized image references for the supported release.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Feast operator and related images build green through the Konflux
  pipeline for the midstream Feast repository.
- The operator-based deployment installs on the platform and reaches a running
  state with its CRDs applied.
- The deployment is consumable by the Platform Operator enablement flow
  (enabling the Feature Store installs/manages this deployment).
- Productized image references are pinned and published for the supported
  release.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1** (P0): administrators can enable a supported Feature Store through
  the Platform Operator, with productized images.

Conditional branch (outcome B of the deployment-topology investigation): if the
standalone-server-per-project topology is selected, productize the Feast server
image and its per-project deployment — one Feature Store server per project —
in the midstream Feast repository. If the investigation selects the
operator-based topology instead, this epic is dropped and that branch applies.

  repository through the Konflux pipeline.
- Carry the per-project deployment resources for the standalone server
  topology, including its endpoint model per project.
- Make the deployment consumable by the Platform Operator enablement
  integration (the managed-component enablement deploys the server per
  project).
- Pin productized image references for the supported release.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Feast server image builds green through the Konflux pipeline for the
  midstream Feast repository.
- The standalone server deploys per project on the platform and reaches a
  running state with reachable per-project endpoints.
- The deployment is consumable by the Platform Operator enablement flow
  (enabling the Feature Store for a project deploys its server).
- Productized image references are pinned and published for the supported
  release.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1** (P0): administrators can enable a supported Feature Store through
  the Platform Operator, with productized images.

# Select the Feast deployment topology to productize first

## Description

Resolves the strategy's open question: whether the supported Feature Store
(Feast) is productized as the operator-based deployment or as the standalone
server per project. Upstream Feast supports both topologies, but their
supportability within the platform differs (upgrade path, multi-project
tenancy, per-project endpoint model, support surface). The answer determines
which productization work exists and how the Platform Operator enablement
integration is approached, so this investigation runs first and gates those
downstream epics. It does not gate the repository, license, or build-pipeline
onboarding, which are identical under both outcomes.

## Scope

- Evaluate both candidate topologies (operator-based deployment; standalone
  server per project) against supportability criteria: upgrade path,
  multi-project tenancy, endpoint model per project, operational support
  surface, and alignment with how the Platform Operator enables other managed
  components.
- Assess upstream maturity of each topology from upstream Feast sources
  (operator and server deployment paths).
- Produce a decision record naming the selected topology, the rationale, and
  the consequences for the Feature Store productization and the Platform
  Operator enablement integration.
- Update the conditional productization plan so the implementing team knows
  which branch applies.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Both candidate topologies are documented with their supportability
  trade-offs, sourced from upstream Feast material.
- A decision record exists that names the selected topology and the rationale.
- The downstream productization scope is determinate from the decision record:
  it unambiguously indicates which conditional productization approach applies.
- The support implications (what Red Hat supports under the selected topology)
  are stated in the decision record.

## HLR Traceability

- Enables **HLR-1** (P0): administrators can enable a supported Feature Store
  through the Platform Operator — the topology choice is a prerequisite for the
  productization and operator enablement work that delivers HLR-1.

# Create the midstream Feast repository under opendatahub-io

## Description

Establishes the productized home for Feast source in the platform's midstream
GitHub organization. The Feature Store is a new component — it has a reserved
Jira component but no productized repository — so this repo-onboarding epic is
the first step of the new-component onboarding chain and everything that builds
Feast artifacts in-repo depends on it.

## Scope

- Create the midstream repository for Feast under the opendatahub-io
  organization, following the conventions of the other midstream component
  repositories.
- Import the upstream Feast source with a documented clone/sync strategy.
- Set up branch conventions, permissions, and repository metadata consistent
  with other supported component repositories.
- Document in the repository README how upstream syncing and midstream
  patching work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The midstream Feast repository exists under opendatahub-io with upstream
  Feast source imported.
- Repository conventions (branching, permissions, metadata) match those of the
  other midstream component repositories.
- The README documents the upstream sync/patch strategy.
- The repository is buildable from a clean clone (source imports and builds
  without out-of-band steps).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1** (P0): the productized repository is the foundation for the
  productized images and deployment that administrators enable through the
  Platform Operator.

# License validation for Feast and its transitive dependencies

## Description

Feast and its Python SDK carry a large transitive dependency tree. Both the
productized Feature Store deployment and the preinstallation of the Feast SDK
in a supported workbench image must be license-cleared before the general
implementation work locks in dependencies. This validation runs in parallel
with repository onboarding (independent inputs) and gates the general
implementation epics that depend on Feast artifacts.

## Scope

- Run license scanning over the Feast deployment artifacts and the Feast SDK
  dependency trees.
- Produce a report of flagged licenses with a disposition for each (approved,
  or remediation required).
- Record a go/no-go statement for productizing Feast and for shipping the
  Feast SDK inside a supported workbench image.
- Where remediation is required, record the remediation plan (dependency
  substitution, upstream patch, or scope change).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A license scan report exists covering Feast and its transitive dependencies
  for both the deployment and the SDK surfaces.
- Every flagged license has a recorded disposition.
- A go/no-go statement exists for productizing Feast and for including the
  Feast SDK in a supported workbench image; if no-go, a remediation plan is
  recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1** (P0): productized images may only ship license-cleared
  dependencies.
- **HLR-2** (P1): the Feast SDK may only be preinstalled in a supported
  workbench image if its dependency tree is license-cleared.

# Onboard the Feast repository to Konflux

## Description

Gives the new midstream Feast repository a build pipeline by onboarding it to
Konflux, so the Feature Store artifacts are built as productized images through
the standard pipeline. This runs after the repository exists and in parallel
with the general implementation work — the pipeline and the code land
concurrently, and the implementation epics carry a "build pipeline green"
acceptance criterion rather than a dependency on this epic.

## Scope

- Create the Konflux application and tenant membership for the midstream Feast
  repository.
- Configure image build pipelines for the Feast artifacts the component ships.
- Wire pipeline status and visibility (PR checks, release builds) consistent
  with other onboarded component repositories.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Konflux application builds from the midstream Feast repository's default
  branch.
- A merged change in the repository produces a runnable image build through
  the pipeline.
- Pipeline status is visible on pull requests in the repository.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1** (P0): the build pipeline produces the productized images that
  administrators enable through the Platform Operator.

# Enable the Feature Store as a managed component in the Platform Operator

## Description

Delivers HLR-1's enablement surface: administrators can enable (and disable) a
supported Feature Store through the Platform Operator, like any other managed
component. The integration approach follows the deployment topology selected by
the topology investigation — enabling a Feast operator, or deploying a
standalone Feast server per project — which is why this epic is gated on that
decision and on license clearance of the Feast dependency tree.

## Scope

- Add the Feature Store to the set of components the Platform Operator manages,
  following the existing managed-component enablement pattern.
- Implement the administrator enable/disable flow for the Feature Store,
  consistent with how other managed components are enabled.
- Align the enablement mechanics with the selected deployment topology
  (operator-based deployment or standalone server per project).
- Validate enablement against the productized Feature Store artifacts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An administrator can enable the Feature Store through the Platform Operator,
  and the component reaches a running, supported state.
- An administrator can disable the Feature Store, returning the platform to its
  prior state.
- The enable/disable flow is consistent with how other managed components are
  enabled (no bespoke operator-specific UX).
- Enablement is validated end-to-end against the productized Feature Store
  deployment for the selected topology.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1** (P0): administrators can enable a supported Feature Store through
  the Platform Operator like any other managed component, with productized
  images.

# Surface the Feature Store in the Dashboard

## Description

Delivers HLR-3's user-facing surface: the Dashboard shows the Feature Store as
an enabled component and links users to its endpoints per project. The
Dashboard reads component state through Kubernetes CRs and owns no data plane,
so this integration consumes the enablement state that the Platform Operator
integration produces. Per the strategy's out-of-scope list, this release is
link-out only — no feature-authoring UI.

## Scope

- Show the Feature Store in the Dashboard's enabled-components view when the
  component is enabled for a project.
- Link users to the Feature Store endpoints per project, using the endpoint
  model of the selected deployment topology.
- Gate the Feature Store surfaces behind the Dashboard's per-component feature
  flag / dashboard-config mechanism, consistent with other components.
- Link-out only: navigation to the Feature Store endpoints, with no
  feature-authoring UI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the Feature Store is enabled for a project, the Dashboard shows it as an
  enabled component.
- The Dashboard links users to the Feature Store endpoints for that project.
- The Feature Store surfaces are gated by the Dashboard's component feature
  flag / config mechanism and default to the supported posture.
- No feature-authoring UI is introduced (link-out only, per the strategy's
  out-of-scope list).

## HLR Traceability
